messages:
maya: Quick sync after the postmortem — captured a short action list to derisk streaming/chat timeouts, partial responses, and reconnect behavior. Keeping this thread lightweight: owners + tiny acceptance criteria.

alex: +1. high-level: reduce client-side retry storms, add short circuit on server for noisy sessions, and add a partial-chunk detector metric.

sara: saw the same pattern in prod yesterday — ~20% of partials correlated with cache thrash when many short sessions hit a cold shard. I'll dig KV TTLs.

jordan: proposing two tactical changes we can rollout this week: 1) client backoff config tweak; 2) server-side transient-circuit that pauses routing for 1s on repeat partials.

alex: client backoff suggestion (for SDKs):\n```json\n{ \"initial_ms\": 150, \"multiplier\": 2, \"max_ms\": 2500, \"jitter\": \"full\", \"max_attempts\": 4 }\n```\nThis should cut retry amplification and keep tail latency under control.

maya: okay owner map draft:\n- Client SDK backoff config + tests -> alex -> target: Wed EOD (acceptance: SDK default applied in canary, no >5% increase in user-visible latencies)\n- KV cache TTL sweep + shard-stability mitigations -> sara -> target: Thu midday (acceptance: reduce cold-shard partials by 50% in replay)\n- Server transient-circuit & telemetry for partial-chunk detection -> jordan -> target: next Tue (acceptance: circuit trips measurable and reduces partial rate on noisy sessions)\n- Canary + rollback playbook -> kelly -> target: before any user-facing rollout (acceptance: rollback < 10m, dashboard green)

kelly: I'll own canary orchestration; will add smoke tests to catch partial-chunk regressions. Planning a canary window 30m with synthetic long-running multi-chunk sessions.

alex: small note — clients should use exponential backoff with jitter rather than fixed retry windows; also prefer a capped jitter to avoid extreme waits for interactive apps.

maya: telemetry items (Jordan/Sara):\n- new metric: partial_chunk_rate per route (labels: model, route, shard)\n- session_stability_score (0-100) computed from handshake/heartbeat/ack gaps\n- retry_amplification_ratio (client retries / successful requests)\n(acceptance: dashboards + alert if partial_chunk_rate > 0.5% on production tier)

jordan: will add tracing tags for chunk sequence id and last-acked-offset so we can reconstruct where partials break. Means some storage schema change but low risk.

sara: FYI there's a recurring pattern at 02:00 UTC where batch resyncs + autoscaler churn correlate with heartbeats missing. I'll add an annotation in the timeline.

maya: mitigation priorities: (1) SDK backoff + jitter, (2) server transient-circuit to stop immediate retries causing further load, (3) telemetry + alerting.

alex: experimental client patch ready, will push to internal-canary now.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: streaming-service v2.14.3-canary -> 2 nodes (tag: partial-detect-experiment).

kelly: running canary smoke — feeding 100 synthetic sessions with intermittent chunk drops. Monitoring session_stability_score and partial_chunk_rate.

maya: quick FAQ: why transient-circuit instead of immediate blocking? because we want a short automatic cooldown on noisy sessions without disconnecting user flows — less user impact, buys time for graceful reconnect.

jordan: implementation note: circuit state is per-session and expires after 1s + randomized jitter; trips after 2 partials within 3s. We'll tune thresholds after canary.

alex: after canary, I'll update JS/Go/python SDK defaults and publish a changelog snippet for customers.

sara: running replay on last 72h logs now to validate cache TTL changes — will post numbers here.

maya: risk log: (1) client default changes could lengthen perceived retry latency for a small % of users — mitigated by canary and opt-in flags; (2) circuit misfires might drop valid sessions — mitigation: short TTL and canary smoke tests.

kelly: canary looks good so far — partial_chunk_rate down 48% in synthetic load, session_stability improved. I'll open the rollout ticket and schedule 1h ramp.

maya: final ask: everyone pls add one sentence acceptance note to the ticket when you finish. We'll reconvene next Fri 10:30am for the post-rollout quick-check.

alex: noted, will add acceptance to SDK PR when merged.

sara: will post replay numbers by EOD.

jordan: infra PR up for circuit + metrics, link: https://git.redwood.dev/r/infra/streaming/23

maya: thanks all. keeping this thread as the single source for owners/timelines. ping me if you need to escalate. :thumbsup:
